profile.reading:
WA13 is one of the data center buildings on Vantage Data Centers' Quincy campus in Grant County, Washington, near the town of Quincy in the Columbia River basin of central Washington. Vantage's own site lists the campus address as 2101 M Street NE, Quincy, WA 98848, describes the site as a 68 acre campus with about 775,000 square feet of data center space split across three buildings, and states the campus carries 89 MW of critical IT load in total. The site names WA11 and WA12 specifically when listing Uptime Institute Tier III certifications, Tier III certification of design documents, Tier III certification of the constructed facility, and Tier III Gold certification of operational sustainability, along with LEED Gold certification from the U.S. Green Building Council. WA13 is not named individually anywhere in Vantage's current public marketing material for the campus, though its location immediately next to WA12 and its place in the sequential facility numbering used across Vantage's North American portfolio make it reasonable to read WA13 as the third of the three buildings the campus page describes, rather than a separate site nearby. That inference is not independently confirmed in this pass, and no building specific certification, square footage, or IT load figure naming WA13 was found in public sourcing, so none is recorded for this building individually.

The reason a data center campus exists in a farming town of a few thousand people in central Washington is electricity. Grant County is served by Grant County Public Utility District, a publicly owned power utility that holds physical rights to 63.31 percent of the combined output of the Priest Rapids and Wanapum hydroelectric dams on the Columbia River, two projects with more than 2,100 MW of combined generating capacity, part of why the region markets itself as having some of the lowest industrial electricity rates in the country. Grant PUD's own public materials describe serving eight data center operators across the county, drawing roughly 280 average megawatts between them, about 37 percent of the utility's total 757 MW system load as of 2025, and state that large power users, including data centers, are billed for the cost of the additional generation and infrastructure their load requires rather than sharing residential rates. The utility also discloses roughly 800 MW of pending large load applications still working through planning, procurement, permitting, and construction, a sign of continued demand pressure from data center developers drawn to the area's hydropower. Grant PUD's materials describe the county's data center customers in aggregate rather than naming individual operators or facilities, so no utility sourced figure specific to Vantage or to this building was found, and none is recorded here as a building level number.

Vantage Data Centers is a wholesale and hyperscale data center developer and operator with campuses across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, and Quincy is one of several Vantage sites in the Columbia Basin hydropower corridor of central Washington, a corridor that also draws other large computing operators for the same utility economics. No Grant County parcel record, construction permit, or occupancy date specific to WA13 was identified in this pass, and no independent trade press coverage naming WA13 individually was found either, so this building's construction timeline and completion date are not recorded here.

reading.body:
WA13 is one of three buildings on Vantage Data Centers' Quincy campus in Grant County, Washington, a 68-acre site in the Columbia River basin near Quincy. Vantage publishes 89 MW of critical IT load for the entire Quincy campus across all three buildings combined, but does not publish a per-building breakdown, so WA13's individual load is not known. Vantage names only WA11 and WA12 individually in its current marketing material; WA13's identity as the third building is inferred from its sequential position in Vantage's facility numbering and its adjacency to WA12, not from independent confirmation.

The campus exists because Grant County is served by a publicly owned utility holding rights to 63.31 percent of the Priest Rapids and Walapum dams' 2,100+ MW combined hydroelectric output. Grant County PUD reports eight data center operators drawing roughly 280 average megawatts combined, about 37 percent of the county's 757 MW total load, and discloses roughly 800 MW of additional large load applications in planning, a measure of continued developer interest in the region's hydropower economics. The utility does not publicly name individual operators or break out per-facility loads, so no utility-sourced figure specific to Vantage or WA13 exists.

The Quincy campus holds Uptime Institute Tier III certifications in design and construction, Tier III Gold certification in operational sustainability, and LEED Gold certification, certifying the buildings for mission-critical hosting with guaranteed uptime and resilience. At the campus-wide 89 MW and 775,000 square feet, the three buildings total roughly 2,150 square feet per megawatt of IT load, a density consistent with hyperscale AI training infrastructure, though no tenant list or per-building figure confirms WA13's specific use. Quincy is Washington's third-largest published data center campus by megawatts, after only two other facilities in a state with 46 mapped data centers.
